summary: Tool data (reports/sta_tool.json) reports passed=true in all 9 corners with setup TNS 0.0 ns, hold TNS 0.0 ns and no DRV violators. Worst setup slack 3.276 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60, op[1] -> _342_); worst hold slack 0.4196 ns (min_ff_n40C_1v95). Typical corner nom_tt_025C_1v80: setup 6.229 ns, hold 0.7754 ns. All worst paths are op-input to register paths. No fix needed; dominant cells cannot be named because the tool data has no per-cell breakdown.
assumptions: All items are owned by Orion (routing/placement fixes) as assigned by the tool; none needs Grid.
An empty drv_violators list means zero max transition, max capacitance and max fanout violations.
Clock frequency for power is the spec's 75 MHz (period 13.333 ns).
Electromigration, dynamic IR, ground bounce, inrush and glitch power are not analyzed by the open flow and are not reported here.
Endpoints _342_, _350_, _351_ are register instances (result or flag flops); their exact bit mapping is not in the given data.
Fix targets (0.147 um line-end gap, 0.54 li density) are derived from the tool policy (5% over min; 90% of max) and are suggestions, not new constraints.
Line-end near-minimum spacing (discrete open/bridge sites) is ranked above density margin because the li windows are still below the 0.6 limit while line ends are direct defect sites.
Low near-limit items are ordered by absolute count of near-limit edges (critical-area proxy) and actionability; li 100% min-width is treated as mostly standard-cell-intrinsic.
Power corners are those reported by the tool: tt_025C_1v80, ss_100C_1v60, ff_n40C_1v95, using sky130A / sky130_fd_sc_hd libraries.
Power numbers are assumed to use post-route parasitics from run run_01M44DR7XRWAQ9XY53AG8SRJCM; the parasitic source is not stated in the input.
Switching activity is the vectorless 0.2 input activity reported by the tool (20% default); no simulation activity (VCD/SAIF) was provided.
The 4.0 ns input/output delays and 0.25 ns uncertainty in the SDC are DEFAULT values pending customer confirmation (spec open_questions).
The 9 corners in the tool data (nom/min/max x tt/ss/ff) are the full corner set from the PDK configuration; min/max are taken to be RC extraction variants.
The IR limit of 0.09 V is the Phase 0 default (5% of 1.8 V nominal supply) as stated in the tool data; the spec gives no power or IR target (power targets are out of scope).
The IR result is assumed to be static (average-current) analysis at nominal 1.8 V; its corner and the net(s) analyzed (VPWR/VGND) are not stated in the input.
The tool report is complete and correct for the GDS at pnr/runs/it1/final/gds/alu8_top.gds; I did not re-run any tool.
Tool severities are authoritative and unchanged; ranking only orders items within and across severities.
Voltage source locations are not given; assumed to be the open flow's default PDN source placement at the macro power pins.

reports/sta_tool.json is the real OpenSTA output for the signoff (post-route) netlist of alu8 with constraints/constraints.sdc; the file itself does not state the netlist stage or whether parasitics (SPEF) were used.
open_issues: Dominant cells on the worst paths cannot be reported: sta_tool.json gives only start, end, type, slack and state per path. A full report_checks with per-cell detail at max_ss_100C_1v60 is needed to satisfy the 'dominant cells' part of A.12.
Electromigration is not analyzed by the open flow; for this small design the risk is expected to be low, but it is unverified.
I/O delay budget (4.0 ns in/out) is a DEFAULT; if the customer gives a tighter budget the op -> register paths are the first to lose slack.
IR result gives no corner, net or voltage source locations; a human should confirm what the IR run covered, and whether ss/ff IR runs are needed.

OpenLane flow power total (0.00020245423365850002 W) does not match the OpenSTA tt_025C_1v80 total (0.0002593128 W); the corner, activity and parasitics behind the OpenLane figure should be confirmed by a human.
Power uses vectorless 0.2 activity; re-run with simulation activity from the verification testbench if a more accurate power figure is wanted.
Worst hold paths (type min) are not listed in sta_tool.json; only hold WS/TNS per corner are available.
density_window_min = 0.0 on all layers; minimum-density compliance is not covered by this report and should be confirmed by the PDK density deck / fill flow.
redundant_via_fits = 0 on all via layers despite many single-cut connections (mcon 852, via 875, via2 79, via3 8); confirm this is layout reality and not a check limitation.
sta_tool.json does not record the netlist stage or parasitics source; REQ-014 requires post-route STA, so the runtime should confirm the run used the routed netlist with extracted parasitics.

messages.summary: Power (OpenSTA 2.6.0, input activity 0.2) totals 0.0002593128 W at tt_025C_1v80, 0.0002075033 W at ss_100C_1v60 and 0.0002985172 W at ff_n40C_1v95. Tool-reported worst static IR drop is 0.000207 V (average 4.54e-05 V) against a 0.09 V limit (5% of 1.8 V). No PDN change proposed. EM, dynamic IR and pad locations are not analyzed by the open flow. Pass/fail is left to the runtime checks.

Ranked all 7 DFM items for alu8. Top risks are the two medium items: 35 met1 line ends at near-minimum spacing (DFM-003) and 7 li density windows at up to 94.9% of the 0.6 max (DFM-001). The 5 low near-limit-geometry items are ranked by absolute critical area and kept informational. No high items; antenna worst 37.33% of limit; no long parallel runs or isolated lines; no locations where a redundant via fits. All data comes from the tool report; I ran no checks myself.

self_assessment.reason: All numbers are copied directly from reports/sta_tool.json and the SDC; margins are large in every corner. Confidence is limited only on path explanation detail, because the tool data has no cell-level breakdown, which is reported as an open issue rather than guessed.
